title: Block: A Monotonic Stack
oneLiner: For each element, find the index of the nearest element to its left that is strictly smaller, with a stack of indices.
keyTakeaway: A monotonic stack pops everything that can never be an answer again before it pushes. Store indices, not values, and get the strict or non-strict comparison right for the question.
explanation:
Return an array where entry i is the index of the closest j < i with nums[j] < nums[i], or -1 if there is none. [3, 7, 8, 4] gives [-1, 0, 1, 0].

Walk left to right with a stack of indices whose values increase from bottom to top. Before handling nums[i], pop every index whose value is greater than or equal to nums[i]: those can't be the answer for i or anything after it, because nums[i] is closer and no larger. The top of the stack, if any, is the answer; then push i. Next Greater Element, Daily Temperatures and Largest Rectangle in Histogram are this block facing the other way or with a different comparison.

starterCode.python:
def previous_smaller(nums):
    # 1. Make a result array and an empty stack of indices.
    # 2. Walk the array left to right.
    # 3. Pop indices while the value on top is greater than or equal to the current value: they can never be an answer again.
    # 4. The answer is the index now on top of the stack, or -1 if it is empty; then push the current index.
    # 5. Return the result.
    return [0] * len(nums)

gotchas: Using > instead of >= when popping, so equal values are wrongly reported as smaller.
Pushing values instead of indices, then having no index to report.

complexity.note: Each index is pushed and popped at most once, so the loop is O(n) overall; the stack can hold all n indices.
